ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is composed of three squares. The largest square is below; a larger upper-left square is placed on the upper left of the largest square; the smallest square is on the upper right and is on the same horizontal line as the bottom side of the upper-left square. In the figure, the top side of the upper-right small square is lower than the top side of the upper-left square, and the vertical distance between the two top sides is marked as 2 cm. The figure also shows that the upper-right small square extends to the right beyond the right edge of the lower largest square, and the exceeding part is marked as 2 cm. Reasoning: The side length of the smallest square is 6 cm. Because the bottom sides of the upper-left square and the smallest square are aligned, and the top side of the upper-left square is 2 cm higher than the top side of the smallest square, the side length of the upper-left square is 6 + 2 = 8 cm. The total width of the two upper squares is 8 + 6 = 14 cm. But the smallest square extends 2 cm to the right beyond the largest square, so the side length of the largest square is 14 - 2 = 12 cm.

method.method_draft: Describe the figure first: the bottom square is the biggest, a square sits directly above its left part, and the smallest square sits to the upper right. Read from the image that the top-left square is 2 cm taller than the smallest square because their bottoms lie on the same horizontal line and the vertical bracket between their top edges is labeled 2 cm. Thus if the smallest side is 6 cm, the top-left square has side 8 cm. Also read from the image that the smallest square extends 2 cm past the right edge of the biggest square. Therefore the width of the biggest square is the combined top-row width minus this 2 cm overhang: 8 + 6 - 2 = 12 cm.
